name: Tee 5-Ball Progression
short_description: Five tee swings per round with one cue rotation. Logs hard-hit rate.
long_description: Hitter takes 5 swings off a tee per round, rotating one cue per round (e.g., 'load', 'see contact', 'finish'). Coach or partner logs each ball as hard-hit, soft, or miss. Two rounds = 10 swings.
setup_steps: Place tee at hitter's front hip
Set 5 balls in a bucket within reach
execution_steps: Hitter takes 5 swings using the round's single cue
Partner logs result of each swing

variations.name: Cue ladder
variations.change: Each round adds a different cue

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Five swings off the tee. Each round you only think about ONE thing — load, see contact, or finish — then we score how many are hard-hit.
kid_friendly.goal: Hit at least 3 out of 5 on the barrel. Loud sound, ball jumps off the tee, you finish balanced.
kid_friendly.why: Your body learns one cue at a time. In a game your brain only has time for one thought before the pitch — this is how we practice that.

name: Front Toss Take-or-Swing (5 pitches)
short_description: Coach calls 'take' or 'swing' mid-toss; hitter executes correctly.
long_description: Coach front-tosses 5 pitches per round. As the ball leaves coach's hand, coach calls 'take' or 'swing'. Hitter must execute the called action and only swing at strikes. Logs decision accuracy and hard-hit rate on swings.
setup_steps: Set L-screen at proper distance for age
execution_steps: Coach front-tosses pitch and calls 'take' or 'swing' on release
Hitter executes call
Log decision + swing result
common_mistakes: Swinging at balls when 'take' was called and pitch was a ball

progressions.change: call replaced by colored ball (red=take, white=swing)

variations.name: Pitch-type decision
variations.change: two-pitch mix (FB/CH); hitter calls pitch and decision

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: I’ll yell ‘swing’ or ‘take’ right when I let the ball go. Your job: do what I called, and only swing at strikes.
kid_friendly.goal: Get the call right 4 out of 5 times. When you swing, hit it hard.
kid_friendly.why: Hitters who chase pitches make outs. This trains your eyes to read the pitch BEFORE your hands decide. That’s how you walk more and crush mistakes.

name: Home-to-First Timed Run
short_description: Standardized home-to-first run with light gates or stopwatch.
long_description: Athlete starts in batter's box, makes a contact-style swing, drops bat in marked zone, runs through first base. Time recorded from contact-equivalent cue to first-base touch. Two reps, full recovery.
setup_steps: Mark batter's box and bat-drop zone
execution_steps: Athlete completes swing motion
Drops bat in zone
Runs through first base
Log time + bat-drop legality
common_mistakes: Throwing the bat outside drop zone

variations.name: Drag bunt to first
variations.change: start from drag-bunt position

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: From the batter’s box, take your swing, drop the bat in the box, and SPRINT through first base. We time both runs.
kid_friendly.goal: Run THROUGH the bag — don’t slow down at first. Try to beat your own time on the second rep.
kid_friendly.why: In a real game, beating out a ground ball is the difference between an out and a hit. The fastest 30 feet of your life happens after contact.

name: Catcher Pop Time to 2B
short_description: Standardized pop time measurement, ball receipt to glove-touch at 2B.
long_description: Catcher receives a thrown pitch and executes throw to second base. Time from ball hitting catcher's glove to ball touching middle infielder's glove at 2B is logged. Three attempts, full recovery between.
execution_steps: Pitch in
Catcher receives + throws to 2B
Time recorded from glove pop to glove pop
coaching_cues: Receive to throw — no extra steps

variations.name: Pop to 3B
variations.change: Throw to third base on bunt fake

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Catch the pitch, no extra steps, fire it to second base. We time from when it hits your mitt to when it hits the middle infielder’s glove.
kid_friendly.goal: Catch-to-throw in one smooth motion. Stop a runner stealing — that’s the test.
kid_friendly.why: Pop time is how scouts measure catchers. Every tenth of a second you save is a runner you can throw out.

name: Reaction Ball Partner Catch
short_description: Bounce reaction ball to partner; track catches in 60 sec.
long_description: Partners stand 8-10 ft apart. One partner bounces a reaction ball off a flat surface to the other. Partner attempts to catch as many as possible in 60 seconds. Switch roles. Logs catches per 60 sec.
execution_steps: Bounce, partner catches, return
Continue for 60 sec
Log catches

variations.name: Pod chase
variations.change: BlazePod variant — see REACTION_POD_HUSTLE

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: This ball bounces crazy on purpose. Bounce it to your partner — they have to catch it however it comes off the floor. Count how many you catch in a minute.
kid_friendly.goal: Beat your last score. Stay low, soft hands, eyes on the ball the whole way.
kid_friendly.why: Ground balls and short hops never come the same way twice. Training your eyes and hands to react fast is what turns errors into outs.

name: 8-Minute Dynamic Warmup
short_description: Standard dynamic warmup gating any throwing or speed work.
long_description: 8-minute dynamic warmup sequence: jog, skips, lateral shuffles, leg swings, lunges, inchworms, arm circles, and band pull-aparts. Must complete before throwing or speed assessments.
execution_steps: Jog 60 sec
A-skip 30 sec
B-skip 30 sec
Lateral shuffle 30 sec each side
Leg swings 10 each
Lunge w/ rotation 8 each
Inchworms x 5
Arm circles + band pull-aparts 30 sec
author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Eight minutes of movement before we throw or sprint. Light jog, skips, leg swings, arm circles — wake everything up.
kid_friendly.goal: Break a light sweat. Feel loose, not tired. Nobody throws or runs full speed until this is done.
kid_friendly.why: Cold muscles get hurt. This is how we protect your arm and legs so you can train at full speed for years, not just one season.

name: Youth Strength Foundations Circuit
short_description: Bodyweight + light load circuit: squat, hinge, push, pull, carry.
long_description: Five-station circuit: goblet squat (light), kettlebell deadlift (light), push-up, inverted row, suitcase carry. 3 rounds x 10-15 reps per station. Technique-first. Supervised. No 1RM.
execution_steps: Rotate through 5 stations
10-15 reps each, manageable load
author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Five stations: squat, deadlift, push-up, row, carry. Light weight. Move slow and clean. Form before weight, every time.
kid_friendly.goal: Finish all three rounds with good form. If your back rounds or you wobble, the weight is too heavy — drop it.
kid_friendly.why: Strong legs, hips, and core make you swing harder, throw harder, and stay healthy. We earn the weight by earning the technique.

name: Acceleration Sprints 10/20 yd
short_description: Short acceleration sprints with full recovery.
long_description: After dynamic warmup, athlete completes 4 x 10 yd sprints then 4 x 20 yd sprints. Full recovery between reps (≥ 45 sec at 10 yd, ≥ 75 sec at 20 yd). Quality over fatigue.
execution_steps: Sprint to cone at full effort
Walk back fully recovered
Repeat

progressions.change: react to coach cue at start

variations.name: Falling start
variations.change: start from forward lean

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Sprint hard to the cone, walk all the way back, then go again. Every rep is full effort — no jogging, no half-speed.
kid_friendly.goal: Your last sprint should feel as fast as your first. If you’re fading, take more rest.
kid_friendly.why: Stealing a base, beating out a hit, chasing down a fly ball — every one is a short sprint from a dead start. This IS baseball speed.

name: Baserunning Reads — 3 Stations
short_description: Three baserunning decision stations: primary lead, secondary read, tag-up.
long_description: Three small stations train baserunning reads: (1) primary lead and back, (2) secondary lead off pitcher's first move, (3) tag-up read on fly ball depth. Coach or partner gives cues; athlete reacts and logs success rate.
execution_steps: Rotate stations
Coach cues, athlete reacts
Log read decision and execution

variations.name: First-and-third
variations.change: double-steal decision drill

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Three stations on the bases. At each one I’ll give you a cue — pitcher’s first move, fly ball depth, pickoff — and you make the right read.
kid_friendly.goal: Right read, right reaction, every time. Not the fastest runner — the smartest.
kid_friendly.why: You don’t need to be the fastest to take an extra base. Great baserunners SEE one thing earlier than everyone else. That’s what we’re training.

name: Infield Triangle Read
short_description: Coach hits 3 grounders per round; fielder shows triangle approach + read.
long_description: Coach fungoes 3 grounders per round (right, middle, left). Fielder demonstrates triangle approach, glove read, and accurate throw to first. Logs clean fields and on-target throws.
setup_steps: Set first baseman or target net
execution_steps: Fungoes 3 grounders
Fielder reads, approaches, throws
Log clean field + throw

variations.name: Short hop only
variations.change: deliberate short hops

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Three ground balls per round — one to your right, one straight, one to your left. Field it clean, then make an accurate throw to first.
kid_friendly.goal: Glove down early, work THROUGH the ball, and put the throw chest-high to first.
kid_friendly.why: This is the most-repeated play in baseball. A clean ground ball plus a catchable throw equals an out — every single time.

name: 60-Second Mental Reset
short_description: Box-breath + cue word reset between pressure reps.
long_description: Between high-pressure reps (live AB, mound visit, error), athlete uses a 60-second sequence: 4-count breath in, 4-count hold, 4-count out, 4-count hold, 4 cycles, then states a chosen cue word. Coach reinforces effort/process language.
setup_steps: Athlete picks cue word at start of season
execution_steps: 4 cycles of box breath
State cue word
Return to play

variations.name: Team reset
variations.change: Whole team breathes together between innings

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Bad pitch, error, strikeout? Step off, four big breaths, say your cue word, and we play the next pitch. That’s the whole routine.
kid_friendly.goal: Use it EVERY time something goes wrong. If you forget, your teammate reminds you. No shame, just reset.
kid_friendly.why: The last play is over. Carrying it into the next one is how a small mistake turns into a big inning. Pros reset in 30 seconds — so can you.

name: Heat-Day Hydration Check
short_description: Pre/post weigh-in and urine-color self-check on heat-index days.
long_description: On heat-index days (>85°F or facility-set threshold), athletes complete pre-practice weigh-in, first-morning urine-color self-check (private), and post-practice weigh-in. Compiler flags athletes who lose >2% body mass and triggers rehydration messaging to athlete and parent.
execution_steps: Pre weight log
Practice
Post weight log
Compiler calculates deficit %
author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Hot day — we weigh in before and after practice, and you check your own pee color (privately) against the chart. That tells us if you’re drinking enough.
kid_friendly.goal: Lose less than 2% of your body weight. Pee should be pale yellow, not dark.
kid_friendly.why: Dehydration makes you slower, weaker, and more likely to get hurt before you even notice. Your body is the best tool you’ve got — take care of it.

name: Bullpen — 15-Pitch Command Block
short_description: Short bullpen, 15 pitches with location targets, logs strike% and arm-zone count.
long_description: Pitcher throws 15 pitches off a mound (or flat ground for 6-8). Catcher sets target for fastball arm-side / glove-side / down. Coach logs strike%. All throws count toward Pitch Smart daily limit.
setup_steps: Coach with target paddle behind catcher
execution_steps: Warmup 8 throws
15 charted pitches
Cooldown stretch
common_mistakes: Pitching to the catcher's body not the glove

variations.name: Mixed counts
variations.change: Coach calls 1-0, 0-2, 3-2 scenarios

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Short bullpen — 15 pitches. Catcher sets a glove, you hit it. Don’t worry about how hard, worry about where.
kid_friendly.goal: Land 9 of 15 in or on the target. Finish each pitch with your chest over your front knee.
kid_friendly.why: Pitchers who throw strikes get to keep pitching. Velo gets you noticed; command keeps you on the mound.

name: Pitcher Fielding — Cover First Base
short_description: Tap-and-cover footwork to first base on a grounder to the right side.
long_description: Coach rolls grounders to 1B; pitcher breaks off the mound on the correct path, runs to a spot 6 feet inside the bag, then turns up the line. First baseman feeds with a soft underhand toss. 6 reps each side of the rubber.
execution_steps: Coach rolls grounder
Pitcher breaks toward foul line then turns up
1B underhand toss; pitcher catches and tags inside of bag
coaching_cues: Catch the ball, then find the bag
common_mistakes: Running directly to bag (gets in 1B way)

variations.name: Comebacker
variations.change: Coach hits at pitcher; pitcher fields and throws to 1B

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Ball gets hit to the right side — your job is to beat the hitter to first base. Take a curved path so you don’t crash into the first baseman.
kid_friendly.goal: Catch the toss before you touch the bag, then run through the inside corner.
kid_friendly.why: Every season a few games end because a pitcher didn’t cover first. Quiet play, big difference.

name: Living-Room Dry Swings
short_description: 10 mirror swings at home, one cue per round, no ball.
long_description: Player stands in front of a mirror at home (or with parent watching) and takes 10 dry swings, focusing on one mechanical cue per round (load, stride, finish). No bat-on-ball; foot speed controlled.
execution_steps: 10 dry swings focusing on one cue
Rest 20s
Repeat with new cue
coaching_cues: Smooth, don’t wreck the living room
common_mistakes: Going full speed in tight space

progressions.change: Add a slow-motion video review after each round

regressions.change: Use a dowel instead of a bat

variations.name: Eyes-closed finish
variations.change: Take the swing, close eyes, hold finish 3s

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Stand in front of a mirror at home. Take 10 slow swings. Each round you only think about ONE thing.
kid_friendly.goal: Finish in the same balanced spot every single rep.
kid_friendly.why: Your brain learns the swing in slow motion, not at game speed. This is the cheat code pros use in the off-season.

name: Living-Room Grip & Forearm Builder
short_description: Towel squeezes and wrist curls at home, 3 sets, no equipment beyond a towel.
long_description: Player performs 3 sets of 15 towel squeezes per hand, then 3 sets of 12 wrist curls holding a water bottle. Builds bat-control and throwing forearm without weights.
setup_steps: Forearm flat on table, wrist over edge
execution_steps: Squeeze towel 15 times each hand
Wrist curls with bottle, palm up then palm down
coaching_cues: Slow down on the way back

variations.name: Slow eccentric
variations.change: 5 seconds on the way down

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Squeeze a rolled-up towel 15 times each hand, then do little wrist curls with a water bottle.
kid_friendly.goal: Finish all 6 sets without your forearms going totally floppy.
kid_friendly.why: Stronger hands = the bat doesn’t move on contact = more hard-hit balls. Cheapest hitting upgrade there is.

name: Living-Room Vision Tracking
short_description: Eye-tracking drill with a tossed ball of yarn — no equipment that can break things.
long_description: Parent or sibling tosses a yarn ball or sock-ball underhand from 6 feet. Player calls 'yes' or 'no' based on whether the ball would have been a strike crossing their imaginary plate. 20 reps.
execution_steps: Tosser flips yarn ball
Player calls 'yes/no' before ball lands
common_mistakes: Watching the tosser's eyes not the ball

variations.name: Number ball
variations.change: Tosser writes 1/2/3 on yarn; player calls number after deciding

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Mom or dad tosses a soft yarn ball. You don’t swing — you just call 'yes, strike' or 'no, ball' before it lands.
kid_friendly.goal: Get 15 of 20 right. Decide early; don’t wait until the ball is past you.
kid_friendly.why: Hitting is mostly choosing the right pitch. Eyes train first; the swing follows.

name: Outfield Drop-Step Ladder
short_description: Drop-step + cross-over to a tagged spot, 8 reps each direction.
long_description: Outfielder starts in athletic stance. Coach points right or left; outfielder executes a drop-step with the called foot and sprints to a cone 15 feet away. Focus on the FIRST step direction.
setup_steps: Set 4 cones in diamond around starter
execution_steps: Coach points; outfielder drop-steps with same-side foot and sprints
common_mistakes: Step toward the ball with the wrong foot first

progressions.change: Coach throws a fly ball after the point

variations.name: Reaction-only
variations.change: Coach uses random hand signal

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Coach points left or right. Your first move is to turn that hip back and sprint — no backpedal, no false step.
kid_friendly.goal: First foot moves in the right direction on at least 12 of 16 reps.
kid_friendly.why: Routes in the outfield are decided in the first step. Wrong step = the ball drops; right step = you’re under it.

name: Outfield Line-Drive Reads
short_description: Coach fungoes line drives; OF calls 'in/out/over' at release.
long_description: Coach hits line drives with a fungo from short distance. Outfielder must verbalize 'in' (charge), 'out' (back), or 'over' (turn and run) at contact. 10 reps. Builds read time before route.
execution_steps: Coach hits; OF calls in/out/over at contact, then makes the play
common_mistakes: Calling after the ball is halfway there

variations.name: Silent read
variations.change: Hand signal instead of voice

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Coach hits a line drive. The second the bat touches the ball, you yell 'in,' 'out,' or 'over' before you take a step.
kid_friendly.goal: Get the right call out loud on at least 7 of 10 balls.
kid_friendly.why: Outfielders who guess wrong on the first read can’t recover. Train your eyes to read off the bat, not the flight.

name: Double-Play Turn — 4-6-3
short_description: 2B feeds SS at the bag, SS pivots and throws to 1B. 8 reps.
long_description: Coach hits to 2B; 2B flips/throws to SS covering the bag; SS receives, pivots inside the bag, and throws to 1B. Focus on footwork at the bag and getting rid of the ball cleanly.
execution_steps: Coach hits to 2B
2B feeds SS
SS receives, pivots, throws to 1B
coaching_cues: Catch and throw in one motion

progressions.change: Add a baserunner sliding into the bag (soft slide)

variations.change: Hit to SS instead

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Take the grounder, one out at second, then fire to first. You and your partner work together — the feed has to be on the chest so the SS can catch and throw in one move.
kid_friendly.goal: Turn 5 of 8 cleanly. No bobbles, no off-balance throws.
kid_friendly.why: A double play is the fastest way out of a rally. Practiced teams turn them; teams that don’t practice it boot the ball.

name: Sacrifice Bunt — 5 Balls
short_description: 5 sac-bunts from front toss, target zone is fair territory near 3B line.
long_description: Coach front-tosses 5 strikes. Hitter squares early, holds bat at top of zone, catches the ball with the bat. Goal: ball stops in fair territory between mound and 3B line.
execution_steps: Square at top of zone
Catch ball with bat angled toward 3B line
coaching_cues: Bat at the top of the zone, never below
Soft hands — give with the pitch

variations.name: Push bunt
variations.change: Target 1B line instead

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Square up early, hold the bat at the top of the strike zone, and ‘catch’ the ball with the bat — don’t poke at it. We want the ball stopped in fair ground near third base.
kid_friendly.goal: 3 of 5 bunts fair and out of the catcher’s reach.
kid_friendly.why: Moving a runner with a bunt is a small play that wins close games. Coaches trust kids who can do it.

name: Cutoff & Relay — 3-Man Chain
short_description: OF → cutoff → tag base. 3 reps each side.
long_description: Coach hits ball to outfielder; OF throws to a lined-up cutoff; cutoff turns glove-side and throws to tag base. Drill the chain at game pace.
setup_steps: Cutoff lined up between OF and tag base
execution_steps: Coach hits gap shot
OF throws to cutoff chest
Cutoff turns glove-side and throws to tag base
common_mistakes: OF throwing on the bounce too early

variations.name: Double cutoff
variations.change: Add a trailer cutoff

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Ball in the gap. Outfielder throws to the cutoff’s chest. Cutoff spins glove-side and fires to the base. Three throws, one chain.
kid_friendly.goal: 4 of 6 chains hit the cutoff’s chest cleanly.
kid_friendly.why: Big throws from the outfield are slower and less accurate than a perfect relay. Teams that relay well keep doubles from becoming triples.

name: Catcher Framing — Low Strike
short_description: 20 low pitches, catcher works the bottom-of-zone receive.
long_description: Coach throws 20 pitches at the bottom of the strike zone. Catcher receives quietly with thumb up and slight upward presentation. Filmed for self-review.
execution_steps: Coach throws low strikes
Catcher receives quietly, holds 1 second
coaching_cues: Quiet body, present the ball, don’t pull
common_mistakes: Pulling the glove up after the catch

variations.name: Corners
variations.change: 10 each at low-arm-side and low-glove-side

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: 20 low pitches. You receive quietly with your thumb up. Don’t pull the ball up — present it, hold it, give the ump a beat.
kid_friendly.goal: 14 of 20 caught quiet, no glove pull.
kid_friendly.why: Umpires reward catchers who don’t move. Steal a few low strikes a game and you save your pitcher’s arm.

name: Catcher Blocking — 3-Ball Sequence
short_description: 3 short-hop balls in a row: left, right, middle. 4 rounds.
long_description: Coach throws 3 short-hop balls in sequence at left, middle, right. Catcher drops to knees, angles hips toward middle, smothers ball with body. Recovery between sequences.
execution_steps: Coach throws short-hop
Catcher drops, angles, blocks
Recover between balls
common_mistakes: Catching with glove instead of blocking

variations.name: Random angle
variations.change: Coach calls direction last second

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Three short-hops in a row — left, right, middle. Knees down, chin tucked, ball stays in front of you.
kid_friendly.goal: Keep 9 of 12 balls within 3 feet of you.
kid_friendly.why: Catchers who block keep runners from stealing free bases. Pitchers throw braver when they trust you back there.

name: Bases-Loaded Live Situation
short_description: Coach hits live; defense reacts to runners and outs. 6 scenarios.
long_description: Set runners at all 3 bases. Coach declares outs (0, 1, or 2) and hits a live grounder or fly. Defense must throw to the right base. 6 scenarios with debrief after each.
execution_steps: Coach calls outs and hits live
Defense executes
30s debrief
coaching_cues: Know the outs before the pitch
Get one for sure, then look for two

progressions.change: Add a wild card pitch (passed ball)

variations.name: Quiz only
variations.change: Whiteboard scenarios, no live ball

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Bases loaded. Coach yells the outs, then hits the ball. You all have to know — before the pitch — where you’re throwing if the ball comes to you.
kid_friendly.goal: Make the right play on 4 of 6 scenarios.
kid_friendly.why: Most youth runs score on mental mistakes, not great hits. Knowing your job before the pitch is half the game.

name: 4-Corner Station Block (15 min)
short_description: Hit / field / throw / mobility stations, 3 min each, 1 min rotation.
long_description: Four stations: tee swings, soft-hands grounders, throwing accuracy, dynamic mobility. Groups of 2-4 rotate every 3 minutes. Keeps everyone moving — anti-line.
execution_steps: Groups rotate clockwise every 3 minutes
common_mistakes: Stations too far apart (wasted rotation time)

progressions.change: Add a 5th station; reduce time to 2 min each

variations.name: Position-based
variations.change: Stations target specific positions

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Four stations, 3 minutes each. Hit, field, throw, move. Coach blows the whistle — you rotate fast and don’t stand in line.
kid_friendly.goal: Hit all 4 stations. No more than 30 seconds of waiting at any one.
kid_friendly.why: You get better by doing reps, not watching them. We pack 4 skills into 15 minutes so nobody’s bored.

name: Reaction Light-Board (Partner Variation)
short_description: Partner flashes hand signals; you react with footwork. 30 reps.
long_description: Partner stands 6ft away and flashes hand signal (left/right/up/down). Athlete reacts with corresponding footwork: shuffle, drop-step, or jump. Measures reaction time and accuracy.
execution_steps: Partner flashes random signal
Athlete reacts immediately
coaching_cues: Stay on the balls of your feet

progressions.change: Add a verbal cue that conflicts with the hand signal

variations.name: Color call
variations.change: Partner holds color cards instead

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Partner shows a hand signal — left, right, up, down. You move that way as fast as you can. No guessing.
kid_friendly.goal: Get 24 of 30 right with no anticipation steps.
kid_friendly.why: Quick first move beats top speed every time. This is the same skill that turns singles into outs.

name: Tee — Oppo-Field 5
short_description: 5 tee swings driving the ball to the opposite field.
long_description: Tee placed slightly deeper in stance. Hitter swings 5 times trying to drive the ball to the opposite-field gap. Builds inside-out swing path.
execution_steps: 5 swings driving the ball to oppo gap
coaching_cues: Knob to the inside of the ball

progressions.change: Mix with pull-tee swings on alternating rounds

variations.name: Inside-half tee
variations.change: Tee positioned more inside

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Move the tee back a little. Try to hit all 5 to the opposite field. Hands stay inside the ball.
kid_friendly.goal: 3 of 5 line drives to the opposite gap.
kid_friendly.why: Hitters who can go the other way don’t get pitched around. It’s how you raise your batting average.

name: Soft-Hands Short-Hop
short_description: Partner rolls 20 short-hops; fielder uses bare hand or alligator-style glove.
long_description: Partner rolls 20 short-hops from 15 feet. Fielder catches with soft, low hands; ball into glove, top hand traps. Builds infield receiving.
execution_steps: Partner rolls firm short-hop
Fielder catches with soft, low hands

variations.name: No glove
variations.change: Use bare hands; tennis balls only

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Partner rolls hard short-hops. Your job is to catch them soft — bring the ball to your belly button. Don’t stab.
kid_friendly.goal: Catch 16 of 20 clean. No double-clutches.
kid_friendly.why: Soft hands are the difference between an out and an error. This is the fundamental that infielders never outgrow.

name: Throwing Progression — Long Toss Build
short_description: Build from 30ft to comfortable max distance, then come back in. ~25 throws.
long_description: Partner throwing progression. Start at 30ft, move out every 5 throws until partner has to one-hop max distance. Then walk back in throwing on a line. Logged as a throwing day.
execution_steps: 5 throws each distance: 30, 60, 90, max
Walk back in, throwing on a line
common_mistakes: Arcing throws on the way back in
Throwing max distance when arm isn’t ready

progressions.change: Add a pulldown phase (5 max-effort throws)

variations.name: Crow-hop
variations.change: Use crow-hop footwork past 60ft

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Start close with your partner, then back up every 5 throws until you’re at your max. Then walk back in throwing line drives.
kid_friendly.goal: Hit your partner’s chest at every distance. Walking back in, throws stay flat — no rainbows.
kid_friendly.why: Throwing far the right way builds a healthier, stronger arm. Throwing far the wrong way is how you blow out an elbow.

name: Overload/Underload Bat-Speed Contrast
short_description: Alternating heavy and light bat dry swings, then a tee finisher. Builds bat speed.
long_description: Hitter alternates rounds of overload (heavier than game bat) and underload (lighter than game bat) swings to recruit faster bat speed, then finishes with game-bat swings off a tee while a partner logs peak exit velo. Three contrast rounds: heavy 5, light 5, game-bat 5 on tee. Built for older players with developed swing foundations.

equipment_substitutions.swap_to: partner logs barrel sound + ball jump

setup_steps: Lay out heavy, light, and game bats in order
Position partner or radar to read the tee finisher
execution_steps: 5 controlled swings with the heavy bat
5 fast swings with the light bat
5 game-bat swings off the tee — log peak exit velo
Rest, then repeat the contrast round
coaching_cues: Stay on plane even with the heavy bat
Let the light bat fly — feel the new top speed
Carry that speed into the game-bat swing
common_mistakes: Swinging the heavy bat so hard the path breaks down
Skipping rest and grinding fatigued swings
Using overload weight that is too heavy for the athlete

progressions.change: dry swings only, no tee finisher
add tee finisher with exit-velo logging
replace tee finisher with front toss

regressions.change: game bat only, focus on smooth max-intent swings

variations.name: Step-back load
variations.change: Add a controlled step-back load to sync timing

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Five swings with the heavy bat, five with the light bat, then five with your real bat off the tee. We measure how hard you hit.
kid_friendly.goal: Make the light-bat swings feel like a whip — then keep that speed on your real bat. Hit the tee ball loud.
kid_friendly.why: Switching between heavy and light teaches your body to swing faster. Faster bat speed is how the ball jumps off your barrel.

name: Swing-Plane Path Check
short_description: Tee placed at three heights to groom an on-plane bat path. Logs hard-hit rate.
long_description: Hitter takes tee swings with the tee set at three heights (low, middle, high) to train a bat path that matches the pitch plane. Partner watches for an on-plane barrel and logs each ball as hard-hit, soft, or miss. One round per height equals 15 swings, with a single mechanical cue per round.
reps_or_rounds: 3 rounds x 5 swings (low / middle / high tee)
setup_steps: Set tee at hitter's knee height for round 1
Have net positioned for line-drive feedback
execution_steps: 5 swings at the low tee with one path cue
Raise tee to belt height, 5 swings
Raise tee to chest height, 5 swings
Partner logs hard-hit result of each swing
coaching_cues: Match the barrel to the tee height
Same on-plane path at every height
common_mistakes: Chopping down on the high tee
Changing the whole swing instead of just the path

progressions.change: middle tee only, groove one path
partner calls a random height each swing

variations.name: Inside/outside
variations.change: Move the tee fore/aft to train path on inner and outer thirds

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: We move the tee low, middle, then high. Your barrel has to match each height with the same smooth path.
kid_friendly.goal: Square up every height — loud contact, ball on a line into the net. At least 3 of 5 hard-hit each round.
kid_friendly.why: Pitches come at different heights. A barrel that stays on plane can cover all of them, so you square up more pitches in games.

name: Numbered-Ball Hand-Eye Tracking
short_description: Hitter calls a number/color on the incoming ball before swinging. Logs read accuracy.
long_description: Coach front-tosses balls marked with numbers or colors. The hitter must call the mark out loud as the ball arrives, then take or swing only at strikes. Trains the eyes to track the ball deep and pick up spin and location before the hands commit. Logs call accuracy and hard-hit rate on swings.
setup_steps: Mark balls with two numbers or colors
Bucket of marked balls within reach
execution_steps: Coach front-tosses a marked ball
Hitter calls the mark out loud, then takes or swings at strikes
Log call correctness and swing result
coaching_cues: See the ball out of the hand
Track it all the way to the bat
common_mistakes: Guessing the call before the ball is readable
Letting the call distract from a balanced swing

progressions.change: call the mark + execute take/swing on strikes only

regressions.change: call color only, no take/swing rule

variations.name: Spin read
variations.change: Mark balls so the spin direction reveals the call

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: I’ll toss balls with numbers or colors on them. Shout what you see, then only swing if it’s a strike.
kid_friendly.goal: Call it right 4 of 5 times and still take a balanced swing at strikes.
kid_friendly.why: The best hitters see the ball early and decide fast. Training your eyes to read the ball is how you stop chasing and start crushing strikes.

name: Ready–Aim–Throw (6U)
short_description: Teach the throw in 3 freeze positions, then throw into open space and collect.
long_description: First-throwing-program drill from the Baseball BC/Rally Cap model. Players learn a throw in three frozen checkpoints — 'Ready' (ball facing out, glove to target), 'Aim' (point glove at target), 'Throw' (release with strong legs). Everyone throws the same direction into an empty outfield, then collects and repeats. Parent helpers correct form at each freeze.
setup_steps: Line players up facing an empty outfield
Give each a bean bag or wiffle ball
Station parent helpers along the line
execution_steps: Coach calls 'Ready' — players freeze with grip checked
Coach calls 'Aim' — glove points at target
Coach calls 'Throw' — players throw into open space
Collect bean bags and repeat
coaching_cues: Fingers across the ball, thumb under
Glove to the target, then throw

progressions.change: freeze at each checkpoint, no throw
throw to a partner 10-15 ft away

regressions.change: bean bag only, 5 ft toss to a parent

variations.name: Coach Says
variations.change: Play 'Coach Says' calling Ready/Aim/Throw positions

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Three magic words: Ready, Aim, Throw. We freeze at each one so you feel it, then everybody throws the same way at once.
kid_friendly.goal: Hit all three freeze spots — grip checked, glove pointed, strong legs — then let it fly.
kid_friendly.why: Every good throw starts the same way. Learn the three steps now and throwing feels easy forever.

name: Show the Dog the Ball (Throwing Progression)
short_description: Arm-action checkpoint: take the ball back so the dog behind you can see it.
long_description: 8U throwing-station progression from Baseball BC. Players work the arm path through four stages — one knee, square-and-throw, stand-and-throw (rock and fire), step-and-throw — checking 'show the dog the ball' (ball faces back, away from the target) at the top of every arm circle. Focus on alignment, balance, and a full arm circle.
execution_steps: One-knee throws checking 'show the dog'
Square-and-throw
Stand-and-throw (rock and fire)
Step-and-throw to finish
coaching_cues: Show the dog the ball at the top
Thumb to thigh, knuckles to sky

variations.name: Partner check
variations.change: Partner calls out whether the dog saw the ball

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Imagine a dog standing behind you. Before you throw, take the ball way back so the dog can see it. Then throw to your partner.
kid_friendly.goal: Show the dog the ball on every single throw. Big arm circle, step to your partner.
kid_friendly.why: A full arm circle makes the ball go farther and keeps your arm healthy. Short, jerky throws are how arms get sore.

name: Alligator Ground Balls
short_description: Two-hand ground-ball technique: glove down, top hand snaps shut like an alligator mouth.
long_description: Foundational fielding drill from the Baseball BC 8U model. Players field rolled ground balls in the 'alligator' position — glove flat on the ground out front, bare (top) hand above it, then both hands snap together and pull the ball to the bellybutton. Roll first, then progress to a gentle fungo.
setup_steps: Partner or coach 15 ft away with a bucket
execution_steps: Roll a ground ball at the fielder
Fielder gets glove down out front
Top hand snaps shut over the ball (alligator)
Pull to the bellybutton, then step-and-throw
coaching_cues: Glove on the ground, fingers down

regressions.change: ball rolled slowly straight at fielder, tennis ball

variations.name: Triangle approach
variations.change: Add a small triangle path to the ball before fielding

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Your glove is the bottom of an alligator mouth — put it flat on the ground. Your other hand is the top. When the ball comes, CHOMP and pull it to your bellybutton.
kid_friendly.goal: Two hands every time, ball pulled to your belly. No one-handed stabs.
kid_friendly.why: Two hands means the ball can’t pop out. This is how every great infielder learned to field clean.

name: Cradle the Catch (Bean Bag)
short_description: Teach soft catching hands: hands out, watch, catch, cradle to the body.
long_description: 6U catching introduction from Baseball BC. Players learn 'Ready – Watch – Catch – Cradle': hands out and together (fingers up for high, down for low, palms out), eyes on the ball, close the hands, then cradle (cushion) the ball toward the body. Start with a self-toss bean bag, then a partner underhand toss.
setup_steps: Each player gets a bean bag
Pair up for the second half
execution_steps: Self-toss the bean bag and catch with both hands
Cradle it toward the body
Progress to a partner underhand toss above and below the waist
coaching_cues: Fingers up high, fingers down low
common_mistakes: Looking away at the last second

regressions.change: hand the bean bag to the player, no toss

variations.name: High/low call
variations.change: Coach calls 'high' or 'low' before the toss

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Hands out, watch the ball all the way, catch it, then cradle it into your body like you’re catching an egg.
kid_friendly.goal: Soft hands — the ball doesn’t bounce out. Fingers up for high catches, fingers down for low ones.
kid_friendly.why: Catching soft means the ball stays in your hands. That’s the whole game on defense — catch it, then make the play.

name: Set Feet, Set Hands, Swing (Tee, 6U)
short_description: Beginner tee hitting built on three setup checkpoints and a balanced finish.
long_description: First hitting drill for the youngest players, from Baseball BC 6U. Coach demos and players mimic three checkpoints — 'set your feet' (strong legs), 'set your hands', 'bat position' — then take 5 swings off a tee with a balanced follow-through ('squish the bug'). Foam/plastic bats only at 6U; bat safety: only swing at the tee, carry the bat by the barrel.
setup_steps: Foam/plastic bats only — no metal at 6U
execution_steps: Coach demo: set feet, set hands, bat position
Players mimic the checkpoints with no bat
Take 5 swings off the tee
Hold a balanced finish each swing

progressions.change: dry swings with no bat, mimic coach

regressions.change: ball on a taller tee, focus on contact only

variations.name: Coach Says
variations.change: Play 'Coach Says' with set-feet / set-hands positions

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Three steps before you swing: set your feet, set your hands, bat ready. Then hit the ball off the tee and finish balanced.
kid_friendly.goal: Quiet feet, good contact, and you don’t fall over on the finish.
kid_friendly.why: Strong, still feet are where every good swing starts. Learn the setup now and hitting gets easier every year.

name: Freeze Tag in Positions (Warm-Up Game)
short_description: Tag game where 'frozen' players hold a throwing or hitting position.
long_description: A fun warm-up game from the Baseball BC 6U plans that doubles as form practice. Players play freeze tag; when tagged, they must freeze in a correct throwing or hitting position until a teammate unfreezes them. Coaches and parents check positions and correct form on the fly.
setup_steps: Mark a safe play area with cones
execution_steps: Players run; taggers tag
Tagged players freeze in a throwing or hitting position
Teammates unfreeze by tagging them

progressions.change: freeze in throwing position with grip
coach calls which position to freeze in

variations.name: Base race tag
variations.change: Frozen players unfreeze by running to a base

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: It’s freeze tag! If you get tagged, freeze in your best throwing or hitting position until a friend frees you.
kid_friendly.goal: Run hard, have fun, and make your frozen position look perfect.
kid_friendly.why: We warm up and practice good positions at the same time — and it doesn’t even feel like work.

name: Relay Throw Race
short_description: Teams line up 20-40 ft apart and race a ball up and back with quick transfers.
long_description: A team throwing game from the Red Sox Foundation and Elkhorn plans. Players form teams of 3-5 in a line 20-40 ft apart. The ball is thrown down the line and back; quick feet and a fast glove-to-hand transfer win the race. Builds catching, throwing, and footwork at game pace in a fun, competitive frame.
setup_steps: Line each team up 20-40 ft apart
execution_steps: On 'go', the end player throws to the next
Ball travels down the line and back
First team to finish the set number of trips wins
coaching_cues: Throwing hand close to the glove
Quick feet into a throwing position

progressions.change: add a turn/relay pivot each catch

variations.name: Around the horn
variations.change: Throw in infield order C-3B-SS-2B-1B

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Two teams, two lines. Race the ball down your line and back. Quick catch, quick throw — fastest team wins.
kid_friendly.goal: Clean catches and fast transfers. Win the race without dropping the ball.
kid_friendly.why: Relays win real games — they get the ball home fast. And racing makes practicing catch way more fun.

name: Run Through First Base
short_description: Hit a wiffle ball off a tee, sprint, and run THROUGH first base.
long_description: Beginner baserunning station from Baseball BC 8U. Player hits a wiffle ball (tee or soft toss), drops the bat safely, sprints, and runs through first base without slowing down, then breaks down. Progresses to rounding first and advancing base to base.
execution_steps: Hit the wiffle ball off the tee
Drop the bat in the zone
Sprint and run through first base
Break down after the bag
coaching_cues: Drop the bat, don’t throw it
Run THROUGH the bag, don’t jump
Hit the front of the base

progressions.change: round first and stop at second
continue base to base to home

regressions.change: no bat — start at home and run

variations.name: Base race
variations.change: Two players race around the bases with a hand-off

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Hit the ball, drop the bat (don’t throw it!), and sprint. Run RIGHT THROUGH first base — don’t slow down or jump on it.
kid_friendly.goal: Full speed across the bag, then slow down after. Hit the front edge of the base.
kid_friendly.why: Running through first means you beat more throws. Slowing down early is how runners get out by a step.

name: Rounding First — Banana Route
short_description: Curved 'banana' path to round first and read the play for an extra base.
long_description: Baserunning-read drill from the Elkhorn 7U-10U plan. Runner drops the bat, takes a curved 'banana' route (three steps out, three steps in) to hit the inside corner of first, chest to the infield, and reads the play. Coach simulates a fielding shortstop or a bobble to teach the read for advancing.
setup_steps: Coach positioned as shortstop with a ball
execution_steps: Runner takes the banana route toward first
Hits the inside corner of the bag
Reads the coach: fielded cleanly (return) or bobbled (advance)
coaching_cues: Three steps out, three steps in
Chest to the infield, eyes on the ball
common_mistakes: Running straight through then trying to turn

regressions.change: walk the banana route to feel the path

variations.name: First to third
variations.change: Extend the read to advancing first-to-third

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: On a base hit, swing out in a little banana curve so you can round first hard and hit the inside corner. Then look at the ball — if they bobble it, you go.
kid_friendly.goal: Smooth banana route, inside corner, and the right read on every rep.
kid_friendly.why: Rounding first the right way lets you grab an extra base when the defense slips. Smart runners score more runs.

name: Fly Ball Communication (Call It)
short_description: Two players track a ball between them and loudly call it until it's caught.
long_description: Communication drill from the Elkhorn 7U-10U plan. Two players line up at least 40 ft apart; a ball is thrown or hit between them on a downward flight, forcing them to call for it ('Ball! Ball! Ball!') until it's secured. Teaches who-takes-priority and avoids collisions and dropped cans of corn.
setup_steps: Coach with a ball between them
execution_steps: Coach lofts a ball between the two players
Both read it; one calls 'Ball!' loudly and repeatedly
The other peels off; caller secures it
coaching_cues: Call until it’s in your glove
If you hear a call, peel off

regressions.change: soft toss between players standing close

variations.name: Priority chart
variations.change: Teach CF-takes-priority and corner-yields rules

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: A ball goes up between you and a teammate. Whoever takes it yells ‘Ball! Ball! Ball!’ until it’s in the glove. The other person gets out of the way.
kid_friendly.goal: Loud, early call every time — no bumping, no dropped easy fly balls.
kid_friendly.why: Two players going for the same ball without talking is how outfielders crash and drop easy outs. Talking keeps everybody safe and the ball caught.

name: Soft Toss — Line Drives
short_description: Partner tosses from the side; hitter drives line drives into a net.
long_description: Classic high-rep hitting drill from the Red Sox Foundation plan. A partner kneels slightly in front and to the side with 5-10 balls and tosses into the strike zone; the hitter drives line drives into a net, screen, or fence, resetting the stance between tosses. Great for grooving the swing and fixing small habits with lots of reps.
setup_steps: Partner kneels to the side with 5-10 balls
execution_steps: Partner shows and tosses into the strike zone
Hitter drives a line drive into the net
Reset stance and repeat
Switch roles after the round

variations.name: Top hand / bottom hand
variations.change: One hand on the bat per round, then both

author: platform

kid_friendly.explain: Your partner kneels to the side and flips you the ball. You hit line drives into the net, reset, and go again.
kid_friendly.goal: Hard line drives — not pop-ups. Reset your stance every toss.
kid_friendly.why: Soft toss gives you tons of swings fast. More good reps is how your swing becomes automatic in games.

author: platform
name: 9-Box Command Grid
short_description: Call a box, throw to it. 18 charted pitches scoring command, not velo.
long_description: The strike zone is split into a 3x3 grid. Before each pitch the catcher or coach calls a box; the pitcher tries to hit it. Score 2 for the called box, 1 for a bordering box, 0 elsewhere. Eighteen charted pitches after a full arm warm-up. Every pitch counts toward the daily Pitch Smart limit.

equipment_substitutions.swap_to: athletic tape grid on a fence or net

setup_steps: Complete the full throwing warm-up before any charted pitch
Hang or tape a 3x3 grid over the strike zone
Catcher in full gear; coach charts with the 9-box card
execution_steps: Coach or catcher calls a box out loud before the pitch
Pitcher delivers to that box
Chart 2 (called box), 1 (bordering box), 0 (anywhere else)
Log the pitch count in the team's pitching board when the block ends
coaching_cues: Miss down, never up and in
common_mistakes: Aiming and slowing the arm down instead of pitching
Chasing a perfect score by shrinking the delivery
Forgetting to log the pitches against the daily limit

progressions.change: Call the box only after the pitcher comes set

regressions.change: Call thirds (up / middle / down) instead of nine boxes

variations.name: Count context
variations.change: Coach names a count first, then a box that fits it

kid_friendly.explain: The zone is a tic-tac-toe board. Someone calls a square, you try to hit it. Nine squares, eighteen pitches.
kid_friendly.goal: Hit the called square on about 4 of every 10 pitches, and keep your delivery exactly the same on all of them.
kid_friendly.why: Anyone can throw it near the plate. Pitchers who can put it where they want are the ones who stay on the mound.

author: platform
name: Towel Finish - Dry Mechanics
short_description: No-ball delivery reps with a towel. Zero throws against the daily count.
long_description: The pitcher holds a small towel like a ball and works the full delivery, snapping the towel at a partner's glove held out front at release depth. Because nothing is thrown, this adds no volume to the Pitch Smart daily count, which makes it usable on rest days and between outings.
setup_steps: Do the normal arm warm-up first, even though nothing is thrown
Partner holds a glove or target at the pitcher's release point out front
execution_steps: Work the full delivery holding the towel
Brush or snap the towel against the target at release
Reset fully between reps
coaching_cues: Same tempo as a real pitch
common_mistakes: Rushing reps together with no reset
Turning it into a max-effort throw

progressions.change: Move the target 6 inches further out front

regressions.change: Start from the stretch with no leg lift

variations.name: Mirror version
variations.change: Face a mirror or film it instead of using a partner target

kid_friendly.explain: Same delivery, but you hold a towel instead of a ball and snap it at a target out in front.
kid_friendly.goal: Reach the target out front every single rep without lunging at it.
kid_friendly.why: It is free work. Nothing is thrown, so it never counts against your pitch limit and you can do it on rest days.

author: platform
name: First-Pitch Strike Game
short_description: Twelve simulated hitters, one pitch each. Tracks first-pitch strike rate.
long_description: The pitcher faces twelve imaginary hitters and throws exactly one pitch to each, resetting fully between them. Only the first pitch matters, which is the pitch that decides most at-bats. Teen bands only, and every pitch is logged against the daily limit.

equipment_substitutions.swap_to: coach behind a net with a target

setup_steps: Coach announces a batter handedness before each pitch
execution_steps: Pitcher comes set as if a hitter is in the box
Throw one pitch, then step off and reset completely
Coach charts strike or ball
Log all 12 pitches to the pitching board
coaching_cues: Strike one is the whole job
Middle of the zone beats the corner
common_mistakes: Skipping the reset and falling into a bullpen rhythm
Adding extra pitches beyond the twelve

progressions.change: Alternate lefty and righty targets each hitter

variations.name: Pressure round
variations.change: The team runs a lap of the bases if the pitcher clears 8 of 12

kid_friendly.explain: Twelve pretend hitters. You get exactly one pitch each, then you step off and start over.
kid_friendly.goal: Throw strike one to at least 8 of the 12.
kid_friendly.why: Hitters are much easier to get out after strike one. Winning the first pitch is the cheapest advantage in the game.

author: platform
name: Changeup Feel - Fastball and Changeup Only
short_description: Twenty pitches alternating fastball and changeup. No breaking balls.
long_description: The pitcher alternates fastballs and changeups for twenty charted pitches, keeping identical arm speed on both. The changeup is deliberately the only off-speed pitch in this drill: it is the secondary pitch youth arms can develop without the elbow stress associated with early breaking-ball use.
setup_steps: Set the changeup grip before the block starts so no time is lost mid-drill
execution_steps: Alternate one fastball, one changeup
Catcher calls out whether the arm speed looked the same on both
Chart strike or ball for each
Log all 20 pitches to the pitching board
coaching_cues: Let the grip take the speed off
Finish out front on both pitches
common_mistakes: Slowing the arm down to take speed off
Slipping in a curveball or slider because the changeup is not working yet
Squeezing the grip so tight the pitch sails

progressions.change: Throw the changeup in fastball counts

regressions.change: Ten pitches, changeup from the stretch only

variations.name: Blind catcher
variations.change: Catcher does not know which pitch is coming and guesses after release

kid_friendly.explain: One fastball, one changeup, back and forth for twenty pitches. No curveballs in this drill.
kid_friendly.goal: Land half your changeups for strikes while your arm moves exactly as fast as it does on the fastball.
kid_friendly.why: A changeup that looks like your fastball is the hardest pitch in youth baseball to hit, and it is a lot kinder to your elbow than a breaking ball.

author: platform
name: Stride Direction Line
short_description: Dry delivery reps along a chalk line to square up stride direction. No throws.
long_description: A line is drawn from the rubber to the plate. The pitcher works the delivery dry and checks where the front foot lands relative to that line each rep. Nothing is thrown, so it adds no volume to the daily count and can be run on rest days or as part of a warm-up.

equipment_substitutions.swap_to: a rope, a bat, or a seam in the floor

setup_steps: Draw a straight line from the rubber toward the plate
Pitcher sets the back foot on the rubber
execution_steps: Work the delivery dry with no ball
Freeze at landing and look at where the front foot is relative to the line
Reset and repeat
coaching_cues: Land on or just inside the line
Front toe closed, not flying open
common_mistakes: Flying open early with the front shoulder
Peeking at the foot before landing

progressions.change: Close the eyes and land, then check the foot

regressions.change: Start from the stretch with a short stride

variations.name: Film it
variations.change: Record from behind so the athlete can see the landing themselves

kid_friendly.explain: Draw a line to the plate, then run your delivery with no ball and see where your front foot lands.
kid_friendly.goal: Land on or just inside the line six times in a row.
kid_friendly.why: If your stride goes sideways, your arm has to fix it. Landing straight is the cheapest way to throw more strikes.

author: platform
name: Receive - Transfer - Throw Footwork
short_description: Catcher receives, transfers and throws to second. 12 max-effort throws, logged.
long_description: Coach flips or throws a ball to the catcher, who receives, transfers to the throwing hand and delivers to second base with clean footwork. Twelve throws total. These are max-effort throws from a crouch, so they carry real arm load and are logged against throwing volume the same way a bullpen is.

equipment_substitutions.swap_to: a cone or glove as the second-base target

setup_steps: Full arm warm-up before any max-effort throw
Catcher in full gear in the crouch; a fielder covers second
execution_steps: Coach delivers a receivable ball
Catcher receives, transfers and throws to second
Time the pop from glove-pop to catch at the bag
Log the 12 throws against the athlete's throwing volume
coaching_cues: Feet under the ball before you throw
common_mistakes: Long, loopy arm action from the crouch

progressions.change: Add a runner so the catcher throws against a live clock

regressions.change: Transfer and footwork only, throw at 60% to a partner 45 feet away

variations.name: Third base
variations.change: Same rep to third instead of second

kid_friendly.explain: Catch it, get your feet under you, throw to second. Twelve throws, timed.
kid_friendly.goal: Same footwork every rep, and a quicker release than last week.
kid_friendly.why: Runners steal on the pitcher's time and the catcher's release. Cleaner feet beats a stronger arm almost every time.

author: platform
name: Block, Recover, Throw
short_description: Block a ball in the dirt, recover it and make a throw. Eight throws, logged.
long_description: Coach throws balls into the dirt. The catcher blocks and keeps the ball in front, then recovers and throws to a base. Blocking comes first: the rep only counts if the ball is kept in front. Under 12, use safety baseballs so the athlete commits to the block instead of flinching.
setup_steps: Full chest protector, mask, shin guards and cup - no exceptions
Arm warm-up before the throwing half
execution_steps: Coach throws a ball into the dirt from 25-30 feet
Catcher blocks and keeps it in front
Recover the ball and throw to the called base
Score containment first, then the throw
coaching_cues: Chin down, chest over the ball
Smother it, do not catch it
common_mistakes: Reaching with the glove instead of blocking
Rushing the throw before locating the ball

progressions.change: Coach varies the angle so the catcher has to block to the side

regressions.change: Blocking only, no throw; balls straight at the athlete

variations.name: Runner going
variations.change: Coach calls a live runner on random reps

kid_friendly.explain: Balls in the dirt. Your job is to keep them in front, then find it and throw.
kid_friendly.goal: Keep 7 of 10 in front. The throw only counts if you blocked it first.
kid_friendly.why: A ball that gets past you moves every runner up. Blocking saves more runs than throwing anyone out.

author: platform
name: Secondary Lead and React
short_description: Time the secondary lead off the pitch and react to what the ball does.
long_description: Runner takes a primary lead, then a controlled secondary lead as the pitch is released, landing on balanced feet as the ball crosses the plate. The coach calls what happened - ball in the dirt, ground ball, fly ball, caught - and the runner reacts. Scored on correct reads, not on speed.
setup_steps: Runners line up at first base
execution_steps: Take the primary lead
Two controlled shuffles as the pitch is released
Land balanced as the ball reaches the plate
Coach calls the outcome; runner reacts and the read is scored
coaching_cues: Land on balanced feet, not stretched out
Eyes on the ball, not the base
common_mistakes: Drifting so far the runner cannot get back
Guessing before the ball is hit

regressions.change: Walk through the shuffle with no reaction call

variations.name: Two-base version
variations.change: Run the same read from second base

kid_friendly.explain: Take your lead, two shuffles as the pitch comes, then react to what the ball does.
kid_friendly.goal: Get 7 out of 10 reads right. Balanced feet every time.
kid_friendly.why: The fastest runner on the team still gets thrown out if they guess wrong. Good reads beat fast legs.

author: platform
name: First-and-Third Reads
short_description: Runners on the corners read the defense and decide. Scored on decisions.
long_description: Runners set at first and third. The coach rolls or points to what the defense does - throw through to second, cut it, look the runner back - and both runners decide independently. This is a decision drill: it is scored on correct choices, not on whether anyone scores.
setup_steps: Place runners at first and third
Coach announces outs and score before each rep
execution_steps: Coach calls the defensive action
Both runners decide and move
Freeze and review: was each decision right for the outs and score?
Rotate runners
coaching_cues: Know the outs before the pitch
Runner at third reads the throw, not the runner
Do not make the first or third out at home
common_mistakes: Both runners moving on the same read
Runner at third leaving on a fake
Not knowing the number of outs

progressions.change: Add a live defense and let the play run out

regressions.change: One runner at a time, coach narrates the read

variations.name: Two outs
variations.change: Re-run every situation with two outs so the rules flip

kid_friendly.explain: Runners on first and third. Coach shows you what the defense does, you decide what to do.
kid_friendly.goal: Make the right call 7 times out of 10 - and always know the outs first.
kid_friendly.why: First-and-third is where games get won and lost. Knowing what to do before it happens is the whole trick.

author: platform
name: Tag-Up Timing
short_description: Read the fly ball, tag at the catch, go. Scored on timing, not speed.
long_description: Runner starts on a base with a fly ball hit or thrown to the outfield. The runner retreats, sets a foot on the bag and leaves at the moment of the catch, not before and not after. A coach at the base calls whether the timing was early, late or right.
setup_steps: Coach stationed at the bag to judge timing
execution_steps: Fly ball goes to the outfield
Runner retreats and sets a foot on the bag
Leave at the instant of the catch
Coach calls early / late / on time
coaching_cues: Watch the catch, not the runner ahead
Foot on the bag, body already leaning
Go on the catch, not the throw
common_mistakes: Leaving early and getting doubled off
Watching the ball instead of the fielder's glove
Standing upright on the bag with no lean

progressions.change: Outfielder throws home so the runner has to beat a real throw

regressions.change: Coach holds the ball up and says 'catch' instead of a live fly ball

variations.name: Shallow vs deep
variations.change: Alternate shallow and deep fly balls so the decision changes

kid_friendly.explain: Fly ball goes up. Get back to the bag, foot on it, and leave the second it is caught.
kid_friendly.goal: Be on time 3 out of 4. Early gets you doubled off; late wastes the whole thing.
kid_friendly.why: A tag-up is free 90 feet. You just have to leave at exactly the right moment.

author: platform
name: Two-Tee Swing Path
short_description: Two tees force the bat through the right path. Logs hard-hit rate.
long_description: A second tee is set just behind and slightly above the ball tee. The hitter must miss the back tee and strike only the ball, which forces the barrel to enter on plane instead of chopping down or uppercutting under it. Ten swings, hard-hit rate logged.

equipment_substitutions.swap_to: a cone stack for the ball and a second cone as the back marker

setup_steps: Set the ball tee at the front hip
Set a second tee (or cone) about a bat's width behind and slightly higher
Clear the swing zone - nobody within a bat length
execution_steps: Swing and strike only the ball
Any contact with the back tee is a miss for that rep
Partner logs hard-hit, soft or miss
coaching_cues: Let the back tee tell you the truth
common_mistakes: Casting the hands and clipping the back tee
Dropping the back shoulder to duck under it
Slowing the swing to steer around it

progressions.change: Move the back tee closer so the window tightens

regressions.change: Use the back tee as a visual marker only, no penalty for contact

variations.name: Inside / outside
variations.change: Move both tees to work the inner and outer thirds

kid_friendly.explain: Two tees. Hit the ball, miss the one behind it.
kid_friendly.goal: 6 of 10 hard-hit without clipping the back tee.
kid_friendly.why: The back tee cannot lie to you. If you keep hitting it, your barrel is taking the long way to the ball.

author: platform
name: One-Hand Isolation
short_description: Top-hand and bottom-hand swings off a tee to isolate barrel control.
long_description: The hitter takes short, controlled swings with one hand at a time, choking up on the bat. Top hand first to feel the barrel turn, then bottom hand to feel the pull through. Light and controlled - this is a feel drill, not a power drill.

equipment_substitutions.swap_to: light_bat or choke well up on a game bat

reps_or_rounds: 2 rounds x 5 top hand + 5 bottom hand
execution_steps: Five controlled top-hand swings
Five controlled bottom-hand swings
Finish the round with two normal two-hand swings to blend the feel
coaching_cues: Short and controlled, never max effort
Palm up on the top hand
Feel the barrel, do not muscle it
common_mistakes: Using a bat that is too heavy to control

progressions.change: Move to a slow front toss one-handed

regressions.change: Dry swings with no ball until the path feels controlled

variations.name: Ball on a cone
variations.change: Use a cone stack so a mis-hit does not jar the wrist

kid_friendly.explain: One hand at a time, choked up, easy swings. Top hand, then bottom hand.
kid_friendly.goal: Clean contact on 7 of 10 without ever swinging hard.
kid_friendly.why: Each hand has a job. Splitting them up is the fastest way to feel which one is not doing it.

author: platform
name: Daily Arm-Care Warm-Up
short_description: The gate before any throwing. No equipment required, adds zero throws.
long_description: A short arm-care sequence run before every throwing session: arm circles, band or towel external and internal rotation, scap squeezes, wrist and forearm work, then easy progressive catch. This is a gate, not a workout - throwing should not start until it is complete, and it adds nothing to the daily throw count.

equipment_substitutions.swap_to: a towel held at both ends, or bodyweight only

setup_steps: Enough clear space to extend both arms
execution_steps: Arm circles forward and back, 10 each
External and internal rotation with a band or towel, 10 each side
Scap squeezes, 10
Wrist and forearm circles, 10 each
Easy progressive catch, starting short
coaching_cues: Finish this before the first real throw
common_mistakes: Skipping it on a cold day - the day it matters most

progressions.change: Add a light band pull-apart set for older athletes

regressions.change: Bodyweight only, half the reps for 6-8

variations.name: Between innings
variations.change: Run the shortened version to stay loose during a long inning

kid_friendly.explain: The short routine you do before you throw anything. Circles, bands, easy catch.
kid_friendly.goal: Do all six every single time, before the first real throw.
kid_friendly.why: Arms that get warmed up properly last whole seasons. This is the cheapest insurance in baseball.

author: platform
name: Accuracy Ladder
short_description: Throw to a target at growing distance. 20 throws, logged.
long_description: Partners throw to a chest-high target, starting close and stepping back one rung each time they hit it. A miss costs a rung. Twenty throws total. Distance is earned by accuracy, which keeps athletes from drifting straight to max-distance throwing.

equipment_substitutions.swap_to: gloves or hats marking each rung

setup_steps: Mark four rungs with cones, starting close
Partners face off at rung one
execution_steps: Throw chest-high to your partner
Hit the target and both step back a rung
Miss and step back in one rung
Stop at 20 throws and log them
coaching_cues: Same arm action at every rung
common_mistakes: Racing to the back rung and airmailing everything
Throwing max effort to reach a distance the athlete has not earned

progressions.change: Add a fifth rung, still gated by accuracy

variations.name: On the move
variations.change: Shuffle two steps before releasing at each rung

kid_friendly.explain: Hit your partner in the chest and you both back up. Miss and you come in a step.
kid_friendly.goal: Earn your way to the back cone. 20 throws, then stop.
kid_friendly.why: Long throws are fun, but nobody cares how far you can throw it if it does not go where you aimed.

author: platform
name: Pre-Pitch Routine
short_description: Build one repeatable routine to run before every pitch.
long_description: The athlete builds a short, identical sequence they run before every pitch - a breath, a look at a fixed point, one cue word, then set. Practising it away from the field means it is automatic under pressure. Deliberately private: no coach scoring, no comparison between teammates.
setup_steps: Pick one cue word that means 'ready' to you
execution_steps: One slow breath out
Eyes to a fixed point
Say your cue word in your head
Set and go
Repeat the exact same sequence ten times
coaching_cues: Short enough to fit between pitches
It is yours - nobody else needs to know it
common_mistakes: Changing the routine when things go badly
Making it so long it does not fit in a real at-bat
Copying a teammate's instead of building your own

progressions.change: Run it in the on-deck circle during a real game

regressions.change: Breath and cue word only, drop the fixed point

variations.name: Defensive version
variations.change: Build the same routine for between pitches in the field

kid_friendly.explain: Breathe out, find your spot, say your word, go. Same four things before every pitch.
kid_friendly.goal: Run it the exact same way ten times in a row.
kid_friendly.why: When a game gets loud and fast, a routine is the one thing you can still control.

author: platform
name: Next-Play Card
short_description: A pocket card with three steps to reset after a mistake.
long_description: The athlete writes their own three-step reset on a small card kept in a pocket or bag: name it, park it, next play. Rehearsed away from the game so it is available in the moment. Private by design - the card is the athlete's, and coaches do not collect or score them.

equipment_substitutions.swap_to: a note on a phone or a scrap of paper

execution_steps: Write step one: name what happened in three words or fewer
Write step two: a physical reset - deep breath, tug the cap, wipe the cleat
Write step three: the one thing to focus on for the next pitch
Rehearse the three steps five times
Keep the card in your bag
coaching_cues: Give it a physical action so your body helps
Next pitch is the only one you can still play
common_mistakes: Writing a pep talk instead of three short steps
Coaches asking to read the cards - the card is private

progressions.change: Use it after a real mistake in a scrimmage and note whether it helped

regressions.change: Coach supplies a sample card to copy and personalise later

variations.name: Team version
variations.change: Agree one shared physical reset the whole dugout uses

kid_friendly.explain: Make a little card with three steps for shaking off a mistake. Keep it in your bag.
kid_friendly.goal: Write your own three steps, then practise them five times.
kid_friendly.why: Everybody makes errors. The players who bounce back fastest are the ones who decided how, before it happened.
